questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Keep driving because you have the right of way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When driving near a truck, remember that trucks:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Stop faster going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Turn in a tighter circle than smaller vehicles.
Pass faster going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and heavier. They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these increases your risk of a crash by distracting you?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving takes your attention off the road. Any of these can increase your chance of a crash.

questions.question: The best safety protection in a crash is:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
A lap and shoulder belt together with an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lap and shoulder belt together with an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts cut your chance of serious injury in half. Airbags add extra protection during a front-end crash when you also wear your seat belt. Use both together for the best protection.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Have your documents ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with both hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with both hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and stay in your car. Tell your passengers to keep their hands visible too. Wait for the officer to ask you for your license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on the road.
Lowering your chance of an accident.
Making you fall asleep.
Making you notice more about other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on the road.
questions.explanation: Worry, anger, fear, and sadness all hurt your ability to drive safely. Stress makes it hard to concentrate. If you are upset, it is better to wait before driving.

questions.question: When entering an expressway behind other vehicles, the most important thing is to:

options.text: Watch the vehicle behind you.
Match your speed and position to fit into traffic flow.
Stay very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Turn off your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Match your speed and position to fit into traffic flow.
questions.explanation: Merge smoothly by matching the speed of traffic. Large trucks cannot always move over for you, so blend in as carefully as possible.

questions.question: City driving is more dangerous than expressway driving because of:

options.text: Lower speed limits.
Narrower driving lanes.
Crossing traffic and pedestrians.
Worse road conditions in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Intersection crashes cause more deaths and serious injuries than crashes on other parts of the road. Always watch for vehicles and people crossing, even if they ignore traffic signals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.
Help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross at crosswalks. Stay alert for children and pedestrians at intersections and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows down your reactions.
Makes you feel more confident.
Gets broken down faster by your body.
Reduces driving mistakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down your reactions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reactions. It also makes you feel too confident and causes you to make more mistakes.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop at any red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends. Traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are upcoming intersections.
There is road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends. Traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on a multi-lane road ends. All traffic in the right lane must move left.

questions.question: As you drive, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
At a red traffic light.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you miss your exit, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly from your lane.
Back up.
Keep driving until you find the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you find the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway. Drive to the next exit or turn-around spot where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway is illegal.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Approach slowly and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn off your radio so you can hear a train.
Only cross when a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Look both ways and listen for trains before crossing. If a flagger is present, obey their instructions.

questions.question: If a traffic officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Do what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a traffic officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of accidents. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Assume all vehicles are the same.
Hide the fact that you do not know the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take time to learn where all the controls and equipment are located.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to learn where all the controls and equipment are located.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, find and learn how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
Makes you fall asleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces your ability to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. In this case, it curves to the left. You may see several of these signs throughout a curve.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches you.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows or stops.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows or stops.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you will not have enough time to stop if the car in front of you suddenly slows or stops. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway begins.
A steep hill is ahead.
The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden beneath the seat.
So the buzzer or light does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should rest comfortably with enough room to fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What will help someone overcome the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime.
Hot coffee.
Fresh air.
Only time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time.
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person get over the effects of alcohol. Nothing else can speed this up.

questions.question: If an approaching train is near or fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully.
Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find a different route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or going fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This is true even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the road carefully and park as far off the road as possible so other drivers can see you. Lift your hood to show your vehicle is disabled.
